key_insight: A monolayer graphene front contact improves current collection and overall efficiency in AlInN/Si nitride solar cells without significantly changing open-circuit voltage.
engineering_relevance: Graphene can serve as a low-temperature semitransparent conductive contact to boost performance in nitride-based photovoltaic devices.
method: Grew AlxIn1−xN on p-type Si(100) with a thin a-Si buffer layer
Tested three Al compositions: x = 0.22, 0.35, and 0.43
Transferred a monolayer graphene film onto the front surface and compared devices with/without graphene under light and dark conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency across all compositions, while open-circuit voltage remained largely unchanged.
watch_item: The study relies on a transferred graphene contact layer, so contact uniformity, process reproducibility, and long-term stability will matter for practical implementation.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
